facts.text: The electric-bus programme can begin carrying passengers 18 months after approval.
facts.interpretation: Strongly supports faster initial deployment of Option A.

facts.text: Option A can increase service frequency on six existing routes rather than concentrating investment in one corridor.
facts.interpretation: Strongly supports wider geographic distribution of benefits.

facts.text: Bus routes can be altered annually as residential and employment patterns change.
facts.interpretation: Moderately supports flexibility under uncertain future demand.

facts.text: The estimated initial capital cost of Option A is 38% lower than that of Option B.
facts.interpretation: Moderately supports lower initial financial commitment.

facts.text: Eighty-two percent of current bus stops already meet the platform requirements for the new fleet.
facts.interpretation: Provides limited-to-moderate support for easier integration.

facts.text: The procurement contract permits vehicles to be added in small batches if demand grows.
facts.interpretation: Provides limited-to-moderate support for incremental expansion.

facts.text: Two neighbouring fictional cities use compatible charging equipment.
facts.interpretation: Weakly supports maintenance and procurement compatibility.

facts.text: A resident survey found slightly higher familiarity with improving bus services than with introducing light rail.
facts.interpretation: Weakly supports easier public adoption; it is not a measure of actual performance.

facts.text: The light rail corridor is projected to carry 46% more passengers per vehicle-hour than the electric-bus programme.
facts.interpretation: Strongly supports higher operating capacity for Option B.

facts.text: Light rail journey times on the planned corridor are projected to vary less during peak congestion.
facts.interpretation: Strongly supports more predictable peak-hour travel.

facts.text: The rail vehicles are expected to remain in service 11 years longer than the battery-electric buses.
facts.interpretation: Moderately supports longer asset life, without alone establishing lower lifetime cost.

facts.text: The central corridor contains 41% of the city's current public-transport boardings.
facts.interpretation: Moderately supports concentrating investment where current demand is highest.

facts.text: The light rail alignment has fully separated lanes for 72% of its length.
facts.interpretation: Provides limited-to-moderate support for protection from road congestion.

facts.text: The rail proposal includes level boarding at every station.
facts.interpretation: Provides limited-to-moderate support for consistent boarding accessibility.

facts.text: A fictional university model predicts modest commercial development near three proposed stations.
facts.interpretation: Weakly supports possible development effects; the estimate is uncertain.

facts.text: A local design survey rated the proposed rail vehicles slightly more positively than the proposed buses.
facts.interpretation: Weakly supports aesthetic preference; it is not evidence of transport performance.
